meta.title: Work Done by a Variable Force: Graphical & Integration Methods

seo.title: Work Done by a Variable Force Graphical and Integration Method JEE Main DPP-036 | SMA Physics
seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering 1D/2D integration of variable forces, force-displacement (F-x) graph signed area calculation, spring work, exact differentials, hanging chain lifting work, and non-conservative closed-loop work.
seo.keywords: JEE Main Physics, Work by Variable Force DPP, F-x Graph Area Work, Spring Potential Work, Exact Differential Work, Work Integration Method, Syed Mazhar Ali, SMA Physics

conceptCapsule.title: Calculus & Graphical Evaluation of Variable Force Work
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. 1D Integration Method: When force varies continuously with position $x$, the total work done is $W = \int_{x_i}^{x_f} F(x)\,dx$. 2. Multi-Dimensional Work: For a 2D/3D variable force $\vec{F} = F_x\hat{i} + F_y\hat{j} + F_z\hat{k}$, total work is $W = \int_{x_i}^{x_f} F_x\,dx + \int_{y_i}^{y_f} F_y\,dy + \int_{z_i}^{z_f} F_z\,dz$. If $\vec{F}$ forms an exact differential ($dW = d(f(x,y))$), the force is conservative and work is path-independent. 3. Graphical Method ($F$-$x$ Curve): Work done equals the net signed area bounded by the $F$-$x$ curve and the displacement axis ($W = \text{Area}_{\text{above}} - \text{Area}_{\text{below}}$). 4. Spring Work: Work required to stretch an ideal spring from extension $x_1$ to $x_2$ is $W = \int_{x_1}^{x_2} kx\,dx = \frac{1}{2}k(x_2^2 - x_1^2)$. 5. Hanging Chain & Liquid Columns: Work required to lift continuous distributed masses to a reference plane is evaluated by tracking the displacement of their center of mass: $W = M_{\text{lifted}} g y_{\text{cm}}$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$W = \int_{x_i}^{x_f} F(x)\,dx = \text{Area}(F\text{-}x), \quad W_{\text{spring}} = \frac{1}{2}k(x_2^2 - x_1^2), \quad W = -\Delta U = U_i - U_f, \quad W_{\text{chain}} = \frac{1}{2}\eta^2 M g L$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When evaluating work from an $F$-$x$ graph, always check the sign of the force: areas where $F > 0$ contribute positive work, whereas areas below the displacement axis ($F < 0$) contribute negative work. For closed-loop non-conservative forces like $\vec{F} = -k(y\hat{i} - x\hat{j})$, work over a full circle of radius $R$ is non-zero and equals $2\pi k R^2$.

questions.statement: A position-dependent force $F(x) = (3x^2 - 2x + 5)\text{ N}$ acts on a particle moving along the $x$-axis. The work done by the force in displacing the particle from $x = 0$ to $x = 2\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$W = \int_0^2 (3x^2 - 2x + 5)\,dx = \left[ x^3 - x^2 + 5x \right]_0^2 = (8 - 4 + 10) - 0 = 14\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The force-displacement ($F$-$x$) curve for a particle consists of a straight line increasing from $F = 0$ at $x = 0$ to $F = 20\text{ N}$ at $x = 4\text{ m}$, and remaining constant at $20\text{ N}$ from $x = 4\text{ m}$ to $x = 8\text{ m}$. The total work done from $x = 0$ to $x = 8\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
Work is the area under the $F$-$x$ graph:
$$W = \text{Area}_{\text{triangle}} + \text{Area}_{\text{rectangle}} = \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 20\right) + (8 - 4) \times 20 = 40 + 80 = 120\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A spring of spring constant $k = 400\text{ N/m}$ is initially stretched by $x_1 = 5\text{ cm}$. The additional work required to stretch it further to $x_2 = 15\text{ cm}$ is:
A variable force $\vec{F} = (2x\hat{i} + 3y^2\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts on a body displacing it from position $(1\text{ m}, 2\text{ m})$ to $(3\text{ m}, 4\text{ m})$. The work done by this force is:
questions.solution:
$$W = \int_1^3 2x\,dx + \int_2^4 3y^2\,dy = \left[ x^2 \right]_1^3 + \left[ y^3 \right]_2^4 = (9 - 1) + (64 - 8) = 8 + 56 = 64\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A force acting on a particle varies with position $x$ as $F(x) = F_0 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{L}\right)$. The work done by this force in moving the particle from $x = 0$ to $x = L$ is:
questions.solution:
$$W = \int_0^L F_0 \sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{L}\right)dx = F_0 \left[ -\frac{L}{\pi}\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{L}\right) \right]_0^L = -\frac{F_0 L}{\pi}(\cos\pi - \cos 0) = -\frac{F_0 L}{\pi}(-2) = \frac{2 F_0 L}{\pi}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is accelerated from rest along the $x$-axis such that its velocity varies with displacement as $v = 3\sqrt{x}\text{ m/s}$. The work done by the net force acting on the particle during its displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 4\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. At $x = 0$, $v_i = 0$. At $x = 4\text{ m}$, $v_f = 3\sqrt{4} = 6\text{ m/s}$.
2. By the Work-Energy Theorem: $W = \Delta K = \frac{1}{2}m v_f^2 - 0 = \frac{1}{2}(2)(6^2) = 36\text{ J}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In an $F$-$x$ graph, the area of the region above the displacement axis represents $+30\text{ J}$ of work, while a triangular region below the displacement axis has a base of $4\text{ m}$ and height $-10\text{ N}$. The net work done during the complete process is:
questions.solution:
1. Area below axis: $\text{Area}_{\text{below}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 10 = 20\text{ J}$.
2. Net work: $W_{\text{net}} = 30 - 20 = 10\text{ J}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A non-linear elastic spring exerts a restoring force $F(x) = -(ax + bx^3)$, where $a = 100\text{ N/m}$ and $b = 400\text{ N/m}^3$. The work done by an external agent to compress the spring by $x = 0.1\text{ m}$ from its natural length is:

A particle moves in the $xy$-plane under the force $\vec{F} = (y\hat{i} + x\hat{j})\text{ N}$. The work done in moving the particle from $(0, 0)$ to $(2\text{ m}, 3\text{ m})$ along any arbitrary path is:
questions.solution:
$$dW = y\,dx + x\,dy = d(xy) \implies W = \int_{(0,0)}^{(2,3)} d(xy) = [xy]_{(0,0)}^{(2,3)} = (2 \times 3) - 0 = 6\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $m = 0.5\text{ kg}$ moves along the $x$-axis subject to a force $F(x) = -kx$, where $k = 50\text{ N/m}$. If the body is released from $x = 0.2\text{ m}$ with zero velocity, its kinetic energy when it reaches $x = 0.1\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$K_f - 0 = \int_{0.2}^{0.1} (-50x)\,dx = \left[ -25x^2 \right]_{0.2}^{0.1} = -25(0.01 - 0.04) = -25(-0.03) = 0.75\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A force $F = \dfrac{c}{x^2}$ (where $c = 12\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2$) acts on a particle on the $x$-axis. The work done by this force in moving the particle from $x = 2\text{ m}$ to $x = 6\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$W = \int_2^6 \frac{12}{x^2}\,dx = \left[ -\frac{12}{x} \right]_2^6 = -\frac{12}{6} - \left(-\frac{12}{2}\right) = -2 + 6 = 4\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A chain of mass $M$ and length $L$ lies on a smooth horizontal tabletop with a fraction $\eta$ ($0 < \eta < 1$) of its length hanging freely over the edge. The work required to pull the hanging part completely back onto the table is:
questions.solution:
Hanging mass: $M_h = \eta M$. The center of mass of the hanging segment is at depth $y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\eta L}{2}$.
$$W = M_h g y_{\text{cm}} = (\eta M) g \left(\frac{\eta L}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\eta^2 MgL$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A force $\vec{F} = -k(y\hat{i} - x\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts on a particle. The work done by this force as the particle completes one full revolution along a circle of radius $R$ in the counterclockwise direction in the $xy$-plane is:
questions.solution:
In polar coordinates: $x = R\cos heta, y = R\sin heta, dx = -R\sin heta\,d\theta, dy = R\cos heta\,d\theta$.
$$dW = -k[y\,dx - x\,dy] = -k[R\sin heta(-R\sin heta\,d\theta) - R\cos heta(R\cos heta\,d\theta)] = k R^2(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta)d\theta = k R^2 d\theta$$
$$W = \int_0^{2\pi} k R^2\,d\theta = 2\pi k R^2$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ moves along the $x$-axis under a conservative force whose potential energy is given by $U(x) = (4x^2 - 16x + 20)\text{ J}$. The work done by the force as the particle moves from $x = 1\text{ m}$ to $x = 3\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
$$W = -\Delta U = U(1) - U(3) = [4(1) - 16(1) + 20] - [4(9) - 16(3) + 20] = 8 - 8 = 0\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The displacement $x$ of a particle of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ as a function of time is given by $x = \dfrac{1}{3}t^3$, where $x$ is in meters and $t$ is in seconds. The work done by the net force acting on the particle in the first $2\text{ seconds}$ is:
questions.solution:
Velocity: $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = t^2$.
At $t = 0$, $v(0) = 0$. At $t = 2\text{ s}$, $v(2) = 2^2 = 4\text{ m/s}$.
By Work-Energy Theorem: $W = \frac{1}{2}m v(2)^2 - 0 = \frac{1}{2}(1)(16) = 8\text{ J}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A liquid of density $\rho$ fills a cylindrical container of cross-sectional area $A$ to height $H$. The minimum work done to pump all the liquid out through a small hole at the top of the container is:
questions.solution:
Total liquid mass $M = \rho A H$. Center of mass of the column is at depth $h_{\text{cm}} = \frac{H}{2}$ below the top rim.
$$W = M g h_{\text{cm}} = (\rho A H)g\left(\frac{H}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\rho g A H^2$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A force $F(x) = \alpha x e^{-\beta x^2}$ acts on a particle along the $x$-axis. The total work done by this force as the particle moves from $x = 0$ to $x \to \infty$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $u = \beta x^2 \implies du = 2\beta x\,dx$.
$$W = \alpha \int_0^\infty x e^{-\beta x^2}\,dx = \frac{\alpha}{2\beta} \int_0^\infty e^{-u}\,du = \frac{\alpha}{2\beta}\left[ -e^{-u} \right]_0^\infty = \frac{\alpha}{2\beta}(0 - (-1)) = \frac{\alpha}{2\beta}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block is connected to two identical springs in parallel, each of stiffness $k$. If an external agent stretches the combination by an extension $x$ from its natural length, the work done on the spring system is:
questions.solution:
Equivalent spring constant: $k_{\text{eq}} = k + k = 2k$.
$$W = \frac{1}{2}k_{\text{eq}}x^2 = \frac{1}{2}(2k)x^2 = kx^2$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along the curve $y = 2x^2$ from $(0, 0)$ to $(1\text{ m}, 2\text{ m})$ under the action of force $\vec{F} = (3x^2\hat{i} + 2y\hat{j})\text{ N}$. The work done by the force is:
questions.solution:
$$dW = 3x^2\,dx + 2y\,dy = d(x^3 + y^2) \implies W = \left[ x^3 + y^2 \right]_{(0,0)}^{(1,2)} = (1^3 + 2^2) - 0 = 5\text{ J}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: An elastic rubber band of natural length $L$ requires a force $F(x) = ax + bx^2$ for an extension $x$. The work required to stretch the band by length $L$ from its relaxed state is:
questions.solution:
$$W = \int_0^L (ax + bx^2)\,dx = \left[ \frac{1}{2}ax^2 + \frac{1}{3}bx^3 \right]_0^L = \frac{1}{2}aL^2 + \frac{1}{3}bL^3$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.
